paper.title: 4DVarNet-SSH: end-to-end learning of variational interpolation schemes for nadir and wide-swath satellite altimetry
paper.conclusion_note: The 42 B16 staging records were checked, but this is not a complete-paper attestation. Twenty B16 records misuse an extraction-review label as experiment_id, one AI interpretation remains NOT_VERIFIED, two legacy records have provenance/path errors, and important paper fields are absent from staging.

claims.extracted_value: Spatiotemporal SSH interpolation from sparse satellite altimetry
claims.evidence_summary: The authors define the task as space-time interpolation of sparse satellite-altimeter observations.
claims.audit_note: Value, task scope, and source are supported.

claims.evidence_summary: The paper evaluates nadir-only and nadir-plus-SWOT observing configurations.
claims.audit_note: Supported, although the broader model input also includes optimally interpolated fields elsewhere in the paper.

claims.evidence_summary: The reconstructed state is SSH.
claims.audit_note: Supported.

claims.extracted_value: NATL60 nature run (NEMO); BOOST-SWOT simulation experiments
claims.section: 3.1 4DVarNet framework; 4.1 NATL60 dataset and case study regions
claims.evidence_summary: The benchmark is BOOST-SWOT and its nature run is the NATL60 NEMO configuration.
claims.audit_note: Composite value requires both locators; neither source was replaced by a secondary summary.

claims.extracted_value: NATL60 model grid 1/60 degree; reconstruction patch grid 0.05 degree
claims.section: 3.4 Implementation aspects; 4.1 NATL60 dataset and case study regions
claims.locator: Patch description and NATL60 opening paragraph
claims.evidence_summary: NATL60 is 1/60 degree; the processed patches use 0.05 degree resolution.
claims.audit_note: The two resolutions refer to different objects and must remain distinguished.

claims.extracted_value: Learned variational data assimilation / unrolled optimizer
claims.evidence_summary: The framework derives a neural architecture from variational DA and an iterative trainable gradient solver.
claims.audit_note: Supported.

claims.extracted_value: Trainable gradient-based solver with convolutional LSTM update operator
claims.evidence_summary: Equation (3) uses a convolutional LSTM to learn gradient updates.
claims.audit_note: Supported.

claims.extracted_value: Predefined sequence of iterative gradient updates
claims.evidence_summary: The neural architecture runs a predefined number of iterative gradient updates.
claims.audit_note: Supported; this is an optimizer unrolling, not a physical time integrator.

claims.extracted_value: Variational observation-mismatch term plus learned-prior consistency term
claims.evidence_summary: The variational cost contains observation mismatch and learned-prior consistency terms.
claims.audit_note: Supported; this inner cost is distinct from the supervised training loss.

claims.extracted_value: Weighted squared SSH state reconstruction error
claims.evidence_summary: The supervised loss includes a weighted squared state-reconstruction term.
claims.audit_note: Supported.

claims.extracted_value: Squared discrepancy between spatial gradients of target and reconstruction
claims.evidence_summary: The supervised loss includes a weighted spatial-gradient discrepancy.
claims.audit_note: Supported.

claims.extracted_value: Prior-operator consistency on target and reconstructed states
claims.evidence_summary: Two loss terms enforce prior encoding of the true and reconstructed states.
claims.audit_note: Supported.

claims.extracted_value: Assimilation-window weights [0, 0.25, 0.75, 1, 0.75, 0.25, 0]
claims.evidence_summary: Equation (9) gives the seven-element weighting vector exactly.
claims.audit_note: Supported.

claims.extracted_value: Supervised training with gap-free simulation targets
claims.evidence_summary: The authors state a classic supervised strategy using gap-free targets.
claims.audit_note: Supported.

claims.extracted_value: Adam
claims.evidence_summary: Adam is explicitly named.
claims.audit_note: Supported.

claims.evidence_summary: Batch size 2 is explicit.
claims.audit_note: Supported.

claims.evidence_summary: Two hundred epochs are explicit.
claims.audit_note: Supported.

claims.extracted_value: 1 GPU small domains; 4 GPUs large domains
claims.evidence_summary: The paper distinguishes one GPU for small domains and four for large domains.
claims.audit_note: Supported because the domain condition is retained in the value.

claims.extracted_value: 4-5 h small domains; 7-8 h large domains
claims.evidence_summary: Training durations are stated separately for small and large domains.
claims.audit_note: Supported; units and experimental condition are preserved.

claims.extracted_value: Variational DA formulation and learned prior; not a claim of primitive-equation residual training
claims.evidence_summary: The variational formulation and learned prior are explicit; the negative PINN classification is an auditor/extractor interpretation.
claims.audit_note: Keep AI_INTERPRETATION and do not promote to an author-reported fact.

claims.extracted_value: Sparse satellite sampling requires spatiotemporal interpolation
claims.evidence_summary: Sparse sampling is presented as the scientific problem motivating interpolation, not as a limitation of 4DVarNet.
claims.audit_note: Correct the field/provenance; do not certify this as an author-reported method limitation.

claims.extracted_value: Extensions to other ocean DA and space-oceanography problems
claims.evidence_summary: The authors explicitly discuss extensions to other DA and space-oceanography challenges.

claims.evidence_summary: The prior uses two residual blocks.

claims.audit_note: Value verified; experiment_id is not scientific.

claims.evidence_summary: Each bilinear unit has two hidden convolutional layers.

claims.evidence_summary: The tensors are seven-day sequences over 240 by 240 pixels, a 12 by 12 degree patch at 0.05 degree resolution.

claims.evidence_summary: The experiments use a seven-day window.

claims.extracted_value: GPU memory limits direct large-domain training
